newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC nod on cutting infotech tariff said likely.
newsitem.headline: APEC nod on cutting infotech tariff said likely.

text.p: Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation members are likely to support a U.S. call for a big tariff cut on information technology products in time for a meeting of the World Trade Organisation in December, a U.S. official said.

An APEC consensus on the issue was likely to be reached in time for the ministerial meeting of the WTO to be held in Singapore in December, John Wolf, head of the U.S. delegation to an APEC meeting in Manila, told Reuters on Friday.

The United States wants APEC's 18 members to reduce tariffs on information technology and related products but some members of the group have initially opposed it on grounds that the U.S proposal has not specified the products.
Wolf is in Manila to attend the fourth and final APEC senior officials meeting before a leaders' summit next month.

The meeting, which began on Friday, aims to reduce the differences among members on how APEC's goal of free trade in the region should be met. Each member has submitted an action plan saying which trade rules they would change.
A Japanese delegate to the meeting who wished not to be named said some Asian countries from APEC wanted electronic home appliances to be included in the U.S. proposal.
"There are strong inclinations in Asia to cover home appliances in the agreement," he told Reuters.
He said most APEC members had agreed that cutting tariffs on information technology would help each of them.
"There is a general understanding to bring down rates, but the details of the agreement have not been worked out," he added.

APEC is comprised of Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
